query_text: Does it matter what we eat?

content.text:
Yes—**what we eat matters a lot**, though it doesn’t have to be perfect or complicated.

Food affects:

- **Energy and mood:** Meals with protein, fiber-rich carbs, and healthy fats tend to keep energy steadier than lots of sugar or highly processed foods.
- **Long-term health:** Eating patterns influence risk for heart disease, type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, some cancers, and obesity.
- **Gut health:** Fiber from fruits, vegetables, beans, lentils, and whole grains supports a healthier gut microbiome.
- **Muscle, bones, and immunity:** Protein, vitamins, minerals, and enough calories help your body repair, fight infection, and stay strong.
- **Brain function:** Diet can affect concentration, sleep quality, and mental well-being.

A simple rule of thumb: most of the time, aim for **mostly whole or minimally processed foods**—vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts/seeds, lean proteins, fish, eggs, dairy or fortified alternatives—and limit **excess added sugar, refined starches, and heavily processed foods**.

That said, **one meal won’t make or break your health**. Overall patterns matter more than perfection. Enjoyment, culture, budget, convenience, and personal needs matter too.
